moves.title: Worked example: ∫ x e^x dx using integration by parts
moves.content: {"schemaVersion":"petros.render.v2","title":"Worked example: ∫ x e^x dx using integration by parts","type":"worked_example","problemStatement":"Compute the integral ∫ x e^x dx by choosing u and dv, applying integration by parts, and simplifying the final answer.","steps":[{"id":"step-1","title":"Choose u and dv","explanation":"Pick u as a factor that becomes simpler when differentiated and dv as the remaining part that you can integrate easily. For integrals like x e^x, choose u = x (because du is simple) and dv = e^x dx (because v is e^x).","predictionPrompt":"Before proceeding, state which choice you would make for u and dv for ∫ x e^x dx."},{"id":"step-2","title":"Differentiate u and integrate dv","explanation":"Differentiate u: u = x ⇒ du = dx. Integrate dv: dv = e^x dx ⇒ v = e^x. These give the pieces needed for the formula ∫ u dv = u v − ∫ v du."},{"id":"step-3","title":"Apply integration by parts formula","explanation":"Substitute into the formula: ∫ x e^x dx = u v − ∫ v du = x e^x − ∫ e^x dx. The remaining integral ∫ e^x dx is straightforward to evaluate."},{"id":"step-4","title":"Evaluate and simplify","explanation":"Compute the remaining integral: ∫ e^x dx = e^x. Thus ∫ x e^x dx = x e^x − e^x + C. Factor if desired: = e^x(x − 1) + C."}],"finalCheck":"Write the final simplified antiderivative for ∫ x e^x dx (include the constant of integration).","sourceGrounding":[{"label":"Integration by parts formula","reference":"Standard calculus identity: ∫ u dv = u v − ∫ v du"}]}
